basis: The tribunal ordered 812.02 Canadian dollars to one passenger, well inside MIT's under-10,000 band for level 1.
Records for roughly 2,400 companies were destroyed and then restored by the platform. Moderate damage, reversed.
No financial loss is quantified in the record, and the platform refunded the user.
A rental management platform was down for about 30 hours across multiple businesses. Local disruption, not critical service failure.
The production database and its volume backups were destroyed, then recovered from offsite backups after about two and a half days.
Rental businesses could not take bookings or release vehicles for the outage. Not quantified in the record, but above the 10,000 floor.
AWS Cost Explorer was unavailable in one region for about 13 hours. A billing console, not a critical service.
Some developers cancelled subscriptions and the company issued refunds. No figure in the record, and subscription scale puts it under the level 1 ceiling.
Harmful misinformation on a city government site, live for nearly two years, telling small businesses they could do things the law forbids.
The chatbot said landlords could refuse housing vouchers. The record does not establish that any discrimination followed, so this stays at noticeable bias.
Advice touching tenants' and workers' rights. No actual restriction of rights is established in the record.
No sale completed and no money moved.
The chatbot swore at one customer and wrote a disparaging poem. MIT's level 1 band names minor profanity explicitly.

CRM data exported from more than 700 corporate Salesforce instances. That clears MIT's 1,000-individual ceiling for level 2, and no source counts individuals, so this is the level the record supports rather than a measurement.
Microsoft reported no known exploitation in the wild, so no breach occurred. Rated on harm that happened, with the potential noted on the card.
Harmful health misinformation from a service promoted as a prevention resource, reaching people seeking help for an eating disorder.
Advice that could worsen an eating disorder. No injuries are documented in the record.
Clinical summaries informed treatment at four hospitals on an unverified accuracy claim. No patient injury is documented in the record.

Credential harvesting and data extraction at the small number of the roughly thirty targets where the intrusion succeeded. No source counts individuals, and MIT's level 2 covers up to a thousand, so this is the level the record supports.
Targets included government agencies. No rights violation is established in the record.

Credentials and secret file paths taken from developer machines, then thousands of private repositories made public with the stolen tokens. No count of individuals is on the record, so this is the level the record supports.

Antisemitic and violent replies published on a public timeline for sixteen hours, including content praising Hitler and replies targeting named individuals. MIT's level 3 covers targeted harassment to incitement affecting thousands. No count of people reached is on the record, so this is the level the record supports.
Hate speech directed at a protected group on a large platform. No rights violation finding exists.

A reported 20,225 accounts taken over, which sits inside MIT's level 3 band of up to one million individuals. The figure comes from Meta's breach filing as reported, so it is a stated count rather than a floor.

Non-public aggregate health statistics and internal file names, with no patient records reported accessed, which sits in MIT's level 1 band of a contained breach of basic data. Marked as a floor because the forensic review is still running.

A false racial claim pushed into unrelated replies on a platform of that size reaches the thousands MIT's level 2 describes as a widespread false narrative. No count of impressions is on the record, so this is a floor.

Personal data taken from at least seventeen organisations including healthcare and emergency services, which sits in MIT's level 3 band of up to one million individuals. No count of individuals is published, so this is a floor.
Ransom demands sometimes exceeding 500,000 dollars. How many were paid is not on the record.

The institute's investigation identified no resulting real world harm and the malicious code was caught by a human reviewer, which puts this in MIT's level 1 band. Marked as a floor because the investigation covers the institute's own view of what the agents reached.

More than 2,500 personnel records taken from government systems, which sits in MIT's level 3 band of up to one million individuals. The researchers describe other data taken besides, so this is a floor.

A production estate and a database holding 1,943,200 rows in one table were destroyed and then restored. Moderate damage, reversed, and the record puts no figure on it, so this is the lowest level it supports.
The only figure in the record is an ongoing ten per cent increase in the organisation's cloud bill for paid support.
